title: Mở đầu một phiên hội thảo
intro: Chủ tọa giới thiệu phiên hội thảo về suy tim: thời gian, diễn giả, cách đặt câu hỏi.
text: Good morning, everyone, and welcome to the second session of today's conference. My name is Doctor Sarah Lee, and I will be chairing this session on heart failure.
We have three speakers this morning. Each speaker will talk for about fifteen minutes. After all three talks, we will have a twenty-minute question and answer session.
If you have a question, please raise your hand and wait for the microphone. Please say your name and your hospital before you ask your question, and try to keep it short.
Our first speaker is Professor James Wong from Singapore. He will talk about new medicines for heart failure. Professor Wong, the floor is yours.

title: Tăng huyết áp ở người trẻ
intro: Một bài nói ngắn về tăng huyết áp ở người dưới 40 tuổi.
text: Today I want to talk about high blood pressure in young adults, people under forty. Many doctors think hypertension is a problem of older people, but this is changing.
In our study, we checked the blood pressure of two thousand office workers in the city. About one in five had high blood pressure, and most of them did not know it.
The main risk factors were eating too much salt, not exercising, being overweight and sleeping less than six hours a night. Stress at work was also common.

So what should we do? First, we should measure blood pressure in every adult, not only older patients. Second, we need to give simple advice about salt, sleep and exercise. The take-home message is simple: check early, and treat early.

title: Phục hồi chức năng tim
intro: Bài nói về chương trình tập luyện cho bệnh nhân sau nhồi máu cơ tim.
text: After a heart attack, many patients are afraid to move. They think exercise is dangerous for their heart. But the evidence shows the opposite.
Cardiac rehabilitation is a programme of supervised exercise, education and support. Patients usually start two to four weeks after leaving hospital, and the programme lasts about twelve weeks.
Large studies show that rehabilitation reduces the risk of another hospital admission by about one quarter. Patients also feel less anxious and return to work earlier.

The problem is that not many patients join. In some countries, fewer than thirty percent take part. The reasons are distance, cost and lack of information. As doctors, we should recommend rehabilitation to every patient before discharge.

title: Hỏi đáp sau bài nói
intro: Một bác sĩ trong khán phòng đặt câu hỏi và diễn giả trả lời. Chú ý cách hỏi lịch sự.
text: Thank you, Professor, for a very interesting talk. My name is Doctor Minh, from a heart hospital in Hanoi. I have a question about the patients in your study.
You said the average age was sixty-two. In our hospital, many heart failure patients are over eighty. Do you think the results are the same for very old patients?

That's a very good question, thank you. To be honest, we had only a small number of patients over eighty, so we can't be sure. In that group, the benefit seemed smaller, and side effects like low blood pressure were more common.
So my advice is to start with a low dose, increase it slowly, and check blood pressure and kidney function often. We are planning a new study only in older patients next year.

title: Rung nhĩ và thuốc chống đông
intro: Bài nói về việc khi nào cần dùng thuốc chống đông cho bệnh nhân rung nhĩ.
text: Atrial fibrillation is the most common heart rhythm problem in adults. It becomes more common with age, and it increases the risk of stroke about five times.
The main question for us is simple: which patients need a blood thinner? To answer it, we use a risk score. It looks at age, high blood pressure, diabetes, heart failure and a history of stroke.
If the score is high, we should start an anticoagulant. Today, the newer drugs are usually the first choice. They do not need regular blood tests, and they cause fewer brain bleeds than warfarin.
However, many patients stop taking their medicine after a few months. So please spend two minutes explaining why the drug is important. A patient who understands is a patient who continues.

title: Sau đặt stent mạch vành
intro: Bài nói về thuốc chống kết tập tiểu cầu kép và lời khuyên cho bệnh nhân sau đặt stent.
text: Every year, more and more patients in our hospital receive a coronary stent. The procedure is quick, but the care after the procedure is just as important.

After a stent, most patients need two antiplatelet drugs. We call this dual antiplatelet therapy. For a stable patient, it usually lasts six months. After a heart attack, it usually lasts twelve months.

The biggest danger is stopping the drugs too early. This can cause a blood clot inside the stent, and that can be fatal. Patients sometimes stop because of dental work or minor bleeding, without asking their cardiologist.
My advice is to give every patient a small card. It shows the date of the stent, the drugs, and a phone number to call before stopping any medicine. It is a simple idea, and it saves lives.

a blood clot inside the stent

title: Thuốc mới cho suy tim
intro: Bài nói về bốn nhóm thuốc nền tảng điều trị suy tim phân suất tống máu giảm.
text: Ten years ago, we treated heart failure with two or three medicines. Today, the guidelines recommend four groups of drugs for patients with a reduced ejection fraction.

One of the newer groups was first developed to treat diabetes. Later, studies showed that it also helps the heart and the kidneys, even in patients without diabetes. It reduces hospital admissions and deaths.
The old way was to start one drug, wait several weeks, then start the next. Now, many experts suggest starting all four drugs quickly, at low doses, within the first few weeks.
Of course, we must check blood pressure, potassium and kidney function. But the message is clear: do not wait. Every month without full treatment is a month of extra risk for our patients.

title: Đau ngực ở khoa cấp cứu
en: Chest pain in the emergency department
intro: Bài nói về cách tiếp cận nhanh bệnh nhân đau ngực ở khoa cấp cứu.
text: Chest pain is one of the most common reasons people come to the emergency department. Most of these patients do not have a heart attack, but we must not miss the ones who do.

The first step is an ECG within ten minutes of arrival. If it shows ST elevation, the patient should go to the cath lab as soon as possible. Our target is less than ninety minutes from arrival to opening the artery.
If the ECG is normal, we check a blood test called high-sensitivity troponin. We repeat it after one or two hours. If both results are low, the risk is very low and many patients can go home safely.
Remember that women, older people and patients with diabetes often have unusual symptoms, such as tiredness or shortness of breath, without strong chest pain.

title: Trình bày poster
intro: Một bác sĩ giới thiệu poster nghiên cứu và trả lời câu hỏi của người xem.
text: Hello, thank you for stopping by. Let me give you a quick overview of our poster. Our study looked at salt intake in patients with heart failure in northern Vietnam.
We asked two hundred patients to complete a food diary for one week. The average salt intake was about twelve grams per day. That is more than double the recommended amount.
The main sources were fish sauce, instant noodles and pickled vegetables. Interestingly, most patients thought their diet was healthy. Only one in four knew that fish sauce contains a lot of salt.
Sorry, could you repeat your question? — How did you measure salt intake? — Good question. We used the food diary and checked urine samples in a smaller group. The two methods gave similar results.
